mainTopic: The disputes between רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא over whether a Torah phrase means רשות (optional) or חובה (mandatory): finishing the case of a כהן and his sister, and starting the case of keeping a כנעני slave forever.
overview: The amud has three parts. First, the גמרא finishes the dispute about "לה יטמא". רבי עקיבא reads the extra word "יטמא" as a חובה for a כהן to bury his sister. רבי ישמעאל says the word only comes along with "לה", and he backs this with his school's rule about repeated passages. Next comes the dispute about "לעולם בהם תעבודו". רבי ישמעאל says keeping a עבד כנעני forever is רשות, because the פסוק is needed to permit buying the son of a non-כנעני father and a כנענית mother. רבי עקיבא learns that permission from "מהם תקנו", so for him the פסוק teaches a חובה. The גמרא then brings sayings about sin: רב חסדא on immorality and anger in the home and on the שכינה leaving Israel, and רבי יונתן and רבי אלעזר on how a מצוה goes ahead of a person and an עבירה clings to him like a dog. Finally, the גמרא returns to the witnesses of a סוטה. It quotes a משנה whose arguments end with one witness for טומאה and two for סתירה. It then rereads the משנה so that the word 'בה' is the source for קינוי and סתירה, and it uses the word 'דבר' to require two witnesses for plain טומאה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא points to the extra word 'יטמא'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains why he reads "לה יטמא" as a חובה. If the פסוק only meant to exclude a limb, the word "לה" would be enough. The extra word "יטמא" must be teaching that the כהן is required to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רבי עקיבא respond? If רבי ישמעאל is right, the Torah could have written "for her" and stopped. Why add "he shall become impure"? Learn from it that becoming impure is mandatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי עקיבא answers רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק about a כהן burying his sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל used the word "לה" to teach that a כהן may become impure for his sister but not for a limb of hers. רבי עקיבא says that lesson only needs "לה". So the extra word "יטמא" is free to teach something new: that it is a חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if your reading is correct
The Merciful One; a name for ה׳ as the Author of the Torah
Let it be silent; let it stop there
Why do I need it? (points to a word that seems extra)
Learn from it; this proves the point

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the general rule that a כהן may not become impure. Here we are talking about a close relative, his sister, where the Torah does allow it. The only question is whether it is allowed (רשות) or required (חובה).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva (how does he respond)?
If so, let the Merciful One write "for her" and be silent;
why do I need "he shall become impure"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:3

phrases.english: Learn from it (that it is mandatory).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — אִם כֵּן, לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion, which comes before this section, of רבי ישמעאל's reading of "לה יטמא" as excluding a limb.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does רבי עקיבא deal with רבי ישמעאל's use of the word "לה"?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "לה" alone would be enough to exclude a limb. The extra word "יטמא" therefore teaches that becoming impure is a חובה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל says the word came along for the ride
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that "יטמא" was written only because "לה" was written. He points to a teaching of his school to explain the repetition.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? Since the Torah wrote "for her", it also wrote "he shall become impure". This follows what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל defends himself against רבי עקיבא's proof from the extra word. He also signals that he is about to bring a teaching to back himself up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל says the word "יטמא" is not a separate lesson. It finishes the phrase together with "לה". So it cannot prove that becoming impure is a חובה. He grounds this in a rule from his school, which is quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Since; because (one thing was written, the other came along with it)
Also
For that which was taught; in line with a known teaching
The school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael (how does he respond)?
Since it wrote "for her", it also wrote "he shall become impure".
This is in line with what the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, אַיְּידֵי דִּכְתַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's argument from the extra word "יטמא".
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the extra word as part of the phrase rather than a new lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word "יטמא" proves that becoming impure is a חובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "יטמא" was written together with "לה", so it teaches nothing about חובה.

steps.title: The rule about repeated Torah passages
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that when a Torah passage is said and then said again, the repetition is only there for something new it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: every passage that was said and then repeated was repeated only for the new thing added in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching that רבי ישמעאל referred to in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this rule, the repeated words about becoming impure are there for one new point: "לה", for her and not for a limb. The other words just come along with the repeated passage. So רבי ישמעאל does not need to find a separate lesson in "יטמא".

keyTerms.meaning: A passage or section of the Torah
Was said and then repeated
A new point that was added

steps.whatToRemember: In the dispute about "לה יטמא", רבי עקיבא reads the extra word "יטמא" as a חובה. רבי ישמעאל says it is only part of a repeated passage, so it is רשות, and "לה" excludes a limb.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Every passage that was stated and then repeated

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִישְׁנֵית אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּתְחַדֵּשׁ בָּהּ.
phrases.english: was repeated only for the new thing added in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the teaching that step 2 referred to.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ישמעאל's claim that "יטמא" is not an independent lesson.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל: a repeated passage is repeated only for its new point.

steps.title: Keeping a Canaanite slave forever: optional or required
steps.stepSummary: The third dispute. On "לעולם בהם תעבודו", רבי ישמעאל says keeping a עבד כנעני forever is רשות. רבי עקיבא says it is חובה, so one may not free him.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Of them you may work with forever": this is optional, says רבי ישמעאל. רבי עקיבא says it is mandatory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case in the same series of רשות-versus-חובה arguments: the עבד כנעני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the פסוק gives permission to keep the slave forever, so freeing him is allowed. For רבי עקיבא, the פסוק is a command, so freeing him is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: "Of them you may take your slaves forever" (ויקרא 25:46)
Optional; permitted but not required
Mandatory; an obligation

steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute decides whether an owner is allowed to free a עבד כנעני at all.

phrases.english: "Of them you may take your slaves forever"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46

phrases.english: is optional; these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.
Rabbi Akiva says: it is mandatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעֹלָם בָּהֶם תַּעֲבֹדוּ — רְשׁוּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the next dispute in the same list of רשות-versus-חובה cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל: keeping a עבד כנעני forever is רשות. רבי עקיבא: it is חובה.

steps.title: What is רבי ישמעאל's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as only optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי ישמעאל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking for רבי ישמעאל's reasoning. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain wording "לעולם" sounds like a command, which fits רבי עקיבא. So the גמרא needs to explain how רבי ישמעאל can read it as only permission.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yishmael?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's view in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי ישמעאל does not read "לעולם בהם תעבודו" as a command.

steps.title: The verse permits buying a child of a Canaanite mother
steps.stepSummary: The Torah commands "לא תחיה כל נשמה" about the כנענים. So the פסוק "לעולם בהם תעבודו" was needed to permit buying the son of a non-כנעני man and a כנענית woman as a slave. Since the פסוק teaches that, it is not a command to keep slaves forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says "you shall not let any soul live", the Torah also needed to write "of them you may take your slaves forever". This permits the case of a man from any of the other nations who had a child with a כנענית woman: you are allowed to buy that child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי ישמעאל uses the פסוק for a different purpose: permitting the purchase of a certain child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the child of a כנענית is included in the command to destroy the כנענים. The פסוק shows that he may be bought and kept as a slave. Because the פסוק is used for this permission, רבי ישמעאל does not read it as a command, so it is רשות.

keyTerms.meaning: "You shall not let any soul live" (דברים 20:16), said about the seven nations of כנען
To permit
A woman from the nations of כנען
You are allowed to buy him

steps.confusionAlert: The child's father is NOT a כנעני; only the mother is. That is exactly why the child can be bought, and why the פסוק is needed.

phrases.english: Since it is written "You shall not let any soul live",
phrases.notes: דברים 20:16

phrases.english: it was also necessary to write "Of them you may take your slaves forever",
to permit (the child of) a man from any of the nations

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבָּא עַל הַכְּנַעֲנִית וְהוֹלִיד מִמֶּנָּה בֵּן,
phrases.english: who lived with a Canaanite woman and fathered a son from her,
that you are permitted to buy him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּכְתִיב ״לֹא תְחַיֶּה כׇּל נְשָׁמָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי ישמעאל's reason for reading the פסוק as רשות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק is needed to permit buying the son of a non-כנעני man and a כנענית woman, despite "לא תחיה כל נשמה". So it is a permission, not a command.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the son of a non-כנעני father and a כנענית mother may be bought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא showing that a child born to a man from another nation and a כנענית woman may be bought as a slave, based on ויקרא 25:45.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: How do we know that if a man from one of the other nations has a son with a כנענית woman, you may buy that son as a slave? The פסוק says: "And also from the children of the residents who live among you, from them you may buy."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up what it just said in step 6 by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא says the son of a non-כנעני father and a כנענית mother may be bought as a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said this child needed a special פסוק, because the Torah commands "לא תחיה כל נשמה" about the כנענים. The ברייתא confirms that the Torah does allow buying such a child. It points to a פסוק that talks about people from other nations who live among us.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה)
The nations, meaning the other non-Jewish nations that are not כנענים
A woman from the כנענים, the nations that lived in ארץ ישראל
Permitted, allowed
The פסוק teaches (introduces the source)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know that, for one from the nations
who had relations with a כנענית woman
and fathered a son with her,
you are permitted to buy him as a slave?
The פסוק teaches:
"And also from the children of the residents
who live among you, from them you may buy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:45

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 6 by showing that a ברייתא allows buying this child as a slave.
steps.raayaObject: That the son of a non-כנעני man and a כנענית woman may be bought as a slave.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that quotes ויקרא 25:45, "וגם מבני התושבים הגרים עמכם מהם תקנו".

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: the son of a כנעני father may not be bought
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a limit: if the father is כנעני and the mother is from another nation, the son may not be bought, because the פסוק says "אשר הולידו בארצכם".
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that even if a כנעני man has a son with a woman from another nation, you may buy that son as a slave. So the פסוק says: "whom they fathered in your land." This means from those born in your land, and not from those who already live in your land.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and sets a limit. If the father is the כנעני, the son may not be bought as a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases look alike, since in each one only one parent is כנעני. The ברייתא shows that the father is what counts. A child is permitted only if his family came from outside and he was born here, not if his father's family was already settled in the land as כנענים.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought (sets up a wrong idea the פסוק will rule out)
They fathered, they gave birth to
Those who are born
Those who live or dwell (here: those already living in the land)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. A non-כנעני father with a כנענית mother is permitted. A כנעני father with a non-כנענית mother is not permitted. The father decides.

phrases.english: One might think that even a כנעני man
who had relations with a woman from the nations
and fathered a son with her,
you are permitted to buy him as a slave;
so the פסוק teaches:
"whom they fathered in your land,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:45, the same פסוק as before

phrases.english: from those born in your land,
and not from those who live in your land.
phrases.notes: "Those who live in your land" means families already settled here, so a son with a כנעני father is left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף הַכְּנַעֲנִי שֶׁבָּא עַל אַחַת מִן הָאוּמּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and sets a limit on the permission from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The limits of the permission: only when the father is not כנעני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words "אשר הולידו בארצכם" in the same פסוק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns this from "מהם תקנו", so "לעולם" teaches חובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gets the permission for the mixed child from the words "מהם תקנו". That leaves "לעולם בהם תעבודו" free to teach that keeping the slave is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? He learns it from "from them you may buy." So why do I need "you shall work with them forever"? To teach that it is an obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא handles the same point. He learns the permission from a different phrase, so the phrase "לעולם בהם תעבודו" can teach his own חידוש: keeping the slave is a חובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי ישמעאל said "לעולם בהם תעבודו" was needed for the mixed child, so it can't be a command. רבי עקיבא answers that the mixed child is already covered by "מהם תקנו". Since "לעולם בהם תעבודו" is now extra, it must be teaching a חובה.

keyTerms.meaning: He derives it, he learns it out
Why do I need it? (asks what an extra phrase is for)
As an obligation, a requirement

phrases.english: And רבי עקיבא?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking: where does רבי עקיבא learn that the mixed child may be bought?

phrases.english: He learns it from "from them you may buy."
So why do I need "you shall work with them forever"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46

phrases.english: To teach that it is an obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִ״מֵּהֶם תִּקְנוּ״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי ישמעאל's reading in step 6 to show how רבי עקיבא's opinion from step 4 still works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבי עקיבא learn the permission for the mixed child?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From "מהם תקנו", which leaves "לעולם בהם תעבודו" to teach a חובה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reads "בהם" as: not with your brothers
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל uses the word "בהם" to teach that only these slaves may be worked forever, and not your Jewish brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? "With them" means: and not with your brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי ישמעאל reads the word "בהם" in the same פסוק. For him it teaches that this rule is for a non-Jewish slave and not for a fellow Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים must explain every part of "לעולם בהם תעבודו". רבי עקיבא draws a חובה from it. רבי ישמעאל reads "בהם" as a limit: a Jew may not be worked as a slave forever.

keyTerms.meaning: With them, meaning only with these non-Jewish slaves
Your brothers, meaning fellow Jews

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל says keeping an עבד כנעני forever is רשות, because "לעולם בהם תעבודו" was needed to permit the mixed child, and "בהם" teaches: not your brothers. רבי עקיבא says it is חובה, because he learns the mixed child from "מהם תקנו".

phrases.english: And רבי ישמעאל?
"With them" and not with your brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״בָּהֶם״ — וְלֹא בְּאַחֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Matches step 9 by showing how רבי ישמעאל uses the word "בהם" in the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי ישמעאל learn from the word "בהם"?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "בהם" teaches: with them, and not with your Jewish brothers.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the ban on enslaving Jews from the end of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא knows a Jew may not be enslaved forever, since he used "לעולם בהם תעבודו" for a different law. It answers that the end of the פסוק says it openly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, where does he learn the law about "your brothers"? It comes from the end of the פסוק: "But over your brothers, the children of Israel, one over another, you shall not rule with harshness."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא learns that Jews may not be enslaved forever. It answers that the last part of the פסוק says this openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 9, רבי עקיבא used "לעולם בהם תעבודו" to teach that keeping a כנעני slave is required. So he cannot use the word "בהם" to exclude Jews the way רבי ישמעאל did in Step 10. He does not need to, because the end of the פסוק already forbids ruling harshly over a Jewish brother.

keyTerms.meaning: The end part of the פסוק
It comes out, meaning it is learned from
Do not rule over him with harshness
Your brothers, meaning fellow Jews

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva: "your brothers" —
phrases.notes: This is a short question: where does רבי עקיבא learn that Jews can't be slaves forever, if he used "בהם" for something else?

phrases.english: it comes from the end of the verse:
"But over your brothers, the children of Israel,

phrases.aramaic: אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו לֹא תִרְדֶּה בוֹ בְּפָרֶךְ״.
phrases.english: one over another, you shall not rule with harshness."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: בְּאַחֵיכֶם — מִסֵּיפָא דִּקְרָא נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the gap left in רבי עקיבא's view after Step 10 gave רבי ישמעאל's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבי עקיבא learn that Jews may not be enslaved forever?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the end of the פסוק, which says openly that one may not rule harshly over a Jewish brother.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל explains why the word "them" is written
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי ישמעאל's approach, the word "בהם" is written as a match to "ובאחיכם".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? Since the פסוק writes "But over your brothers," it also writes "them."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי ישמעאל and explains why the פסוק writes the word "בהם". Since it writes "ובאחיכם" about Jews, it also writes "בהם" about the slaves as a matching contrast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק already forbids enslaving Jews, so the word "בהם" might look extra. The איידי answer says "בהם" was written only because "ובאחיכם" was written next to it, so it does not need a separate lesson of its own. The next step gives a rule that backs this up.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is written, meaning because one word is written, the matching word is written too
It also writes
"Them," meaning the non-Jewish slaves

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yishmael:
since it is written "But over your brothers,"
it also writes "them."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: אַיְּידֵי דִּכְתִיב ״וּבְאַחֵיכֶם״, כְּתִיב נָמֵי ״בָּהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 11 explained רבי עקיבא, this step explains the wording of the פסוק under רבי ישמעאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the word "בהם" written if the end of the פסוק already protects Jews?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "בהם" is written to match "ובאחיכם", setting slaves and Jewish brothers side by side.

steps.title: The rule that a repeated passage comes to teach something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the previous answer with a rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל. When a passage is said and then repeated, it is repeated only because of a new detail in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught. As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: every passage that was said and then repeated was repeated only for the new thing added in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a general rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל. When the Torah repeats a topic, the repetition is there because of something new in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of slaves were already taught, and they are repeated here because of a new point: a non-Jewish slave may be kept forever. The word "בהם" comes along with that repeated passage, so it does not need to teach a lesson of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: The school, or study hall, of רבי ישמעאל
Said and then repeated
A new detail that was added

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא learns that Jews may not be enslaved forever from the end of the פסוק. Under רבי ישמעאל, the word "בהם" is written only because "ובאחיכם" is written next to it. A repeated passage always comes to teach something new.

steps.title: Immorality and anger eat away at a home
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that immoral behavior and anger in a home ruin it slowly, like a worm eating sesame.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Immoral behavior in a home is like a worm in sesame. And רב חסדא said: Anger in a home is like a worm in sesame.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section of sayings by רב חסדא about sin. He compares immorality and anger in a home to a worm that eats sesame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A worm in sesame does its damage quietly from the inside until the crop is ruined. In the same way, immorality and anger slowly destroy a home. This connects to the topic of the מסכתא, which deals with a suspicion of immorality.

keyTerms.meaning: Immoral behavior
Anger, harshness
A worm

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The slave discussion has ended, and the גמרא now brings sayings of רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Immorality and anger in a home slowly destroy it, like a worm in sesame.

steps.title: Both sayings are about the woman of the house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב חסדא's two sayings. They refer to the woman of the house, and with a man the damage is not as great.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both this and that are said about the woman. But with a man, we are not concerned about it to the same degree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא clarifies who רב חסדא was talking about. Both sayings are about the woman of the house, not the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the scope of the two sayings. It does not mean the behavior is fine for a man. It means the extreme "worm in sesame" damage happens when it comes from the woman, because her role holds the home together.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that
A woman
A man
We are not concerned about it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying immorality or anger is allowed for a man. The גמרא only says the home-destroying result described here is tied to the woman.

phrases.english: Both this and that are about the woman,
but with a man, we are not concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי בְּאִיתְּתָא, אֲבָל בְּגַבְרָא לֵית לַן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the two sayings of רב חסדא in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The destructive effect described applies when the woman of the house behaves this way.

steps.title: The Divine Presence left Israel when they sinned
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that before the Jews sinned, the שכינה rested with each one of them. After they sinned, it left them. Both parts are learned from one פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: At first, before the Jews sinned, the שכינה rested with each and every one, as it says, "For ה׳ your God walks in the midst of your camp." Once they sinned, the שכינה left them, as it says, "That He not see an unseemly thing in you and turn away from you."
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives another teaching about sin. Sin caused the שכינה, which once rested with every Jew, to leave them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both proofs come from the same פסוק. The first half shows that ה׳ walks among the camp. The second half warns that an "unseemly thing" makes Him turn away. This ties sin, and especially immorality, to losing the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Divine Presence
Rests, dwells
Left, withdrew
An unseemly or indecent thing

steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא teaches that immorality and anger destroy a home, mainly when they come from the woman. Sin drove away the שכינה, which once rested with each Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another saying of רב חסדא about what sin does, continuing the series begun in Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before sin, the שכינה rested with every Jew. Sin caused it to leave.

steps.title: A מצוה walks ahead of you, a sin wraps around you
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יונתן, teaches that even one מצוה goes ahead of a person to עולם הבא, and even one עבירה wraps around him and goes ahead of him to יום הדין. Each half is learned from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: Whoever does one מצוה in this world, it goes ahead of him and walks in front of him to עולם הבא, as the פסוק says: 'And your righteousness shall go before you.' And whoever does one עבירה in this world, it wraps around him and walks in front of him to יום הדין, as the פסוק says: 'The paths of their way wind around; they go up into emptiness and are lost.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another אגדה teaching, following the sayings of רב חסדא. It teaches that what a person does in this world goes with him into the next world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two matching halves. A מצוה walks ahead of you like an escort to עולם הבא, and an עבירה clings to you and walks ahead of you to judgment. The second פסוק uses the word יִלָּפְתוּ, which connects to מְלַפַּפְתּוֹ, 'wraps around him.'

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment, a good deed done for ה'
A sin, crossing a line the תורה set
The World-to-Come
The Day of Judgment
It wraps around him, clings to him

Rabbi Yonatan said:

it goes ahead of him and walks before him to the World-to-Come,
as it says: 'And your righteousness shall go before you.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה 58:8

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one מצוה escorts a person to עולם הבא, and even one עבירה clings to him and goes before him to יום הדין.

steps.title: A sin is tied to a person like a dog
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says an עבירה is tied to a person like a dog. He learns it from the פסוק about יוסף refusing אשת פוטיפר: 'to lie by her' in this world would have meant 'to be with her' in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: The sin is tied to him like a dog, as the verse says: 'He did not listen to her, to lie by her, to be with her.' 'To lie by her' means in this world; 'to be with her' means in the World-to-Come.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר adds his own picture to the idea that a sin follows a person: it is tied to him like a dog on a leash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to repeat itself with two phrases. רבי אלעזר reads them as two different times: a short sin in this world would have left יוסף tied to it forever in the next world. A dog that is tied to you never leaves your side.

keyTerms.meaning: Tied to him
Like a dog
To be with her, read here as forever, in the next world

steps.whatToRemember: A מצוה walks ahead of you to עולם הבא. An עבירה wraps around you and stays tied to you like a dog, even into the next world.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:
It is tied to him like a dog,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the sin from the previous step.

phrases.english: as it says: 'And he did not listen to her,
phrases.notes: בראשית 39:10, about יוסף and the wife of פוטיפר.

phrases.english: to lie by her, to be with her.'
'To lie by her' means in this world;
'to be with her' means in the World-to-Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: קְשׁוּרָה בּוֹ כְּכֶלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second picture of how an עבירה stays with a person, building on רבי יונתן's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבירה stays tied to a person like a dog, from this world into the next.

steps.title: Logic says one witness should not be enough to prove defilement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the halachic topic of witnesses. It quotes a משנה from later in the מסכתא with a קל וחומר: the first testimony, about סתירה, can be undone and still needs two witnesses. So the final testimony, about טומאה, which forbids her forever, should surely need two.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: 'For logic would have said: If the first testimony, which does not forbid her forever, is not accepted with fewer than two witnesses, then the last testimony, which does forbid her forever, should certainly not be accepted with fewer than two!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the אגדה and returns to the topic of how many עדים are needed for a סוטה. It quotes a משנה that sets up a logical argument, preparing the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first testimony' is about סתירה, being alone with the man. It does not forbid her forever, because she can drink the bitter water and go back to her husband. The 'last testimony' is about טומאה, actual sin, which forbids her forever. A more serious result should need at least as much proof, so it should need two witnesses too.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere
Logic would have said, a way of opening a קל וחומר
The first testimony, about סתירה
The last testimony, about טומאה
A permanent prohibition, she can never return to her husband

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final halacha. The משנה brings this logic only to show why it needed a special source to teach that one witness IS believed about טומאה. The answer comes next.
steps.whyThisMatters: This argument sets up the question of why one witness is believed about טומאה, which the גמרא is about to discuss.

phrases.english: We learned there, in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: This משנה is later in the מסכתא (31a), about one witness who says she sinned.

phrases.english: For logic would have said:
Just as the first testimony,
phrases.notes: The 'first testimony' is about סתירה, that she was alone with the man.

phrases.english: which does not forbid her forever,
is not accepted with fewer than two witnesses,
then the last testimony,
phrases.notes: The 'last testimony' is that she actually sinned (טומאה).

phrases.english: which does forbid her forever,
is it not logical that it should not be accepted
with fewer than two witnesses?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם, שֶׁהָיָה בַּדִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה section and returns to the earlier halachic discussion about how many witnesses each stage of the סוטה process needs
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A quoted משנה argues by קל וחומר that testimony of טומאה, which forbids her forever, should need two witnesses, just like testimony of סתירה.

steps.title: The verse shows one witness is enough for טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה blocks the קל וחומר from step 19. The פסוק 'ועד אין בה' teaches that any testimony against her, even one witness, is enough for טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And there is no witness against her.' This means any testimony there is against her is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the קל וחומר from step 19, which said טומאה should need two witnesses. A פסוק shows that one witness is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic said that the final testimony, which forbids her forever, should need at least two witnesses. The פסוק overrides that logic: 'ועד אין בה' means there were not two witnesses, only one, and that is still enough. A clear verse beats a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (used to show a פסוק overrides logic)
'And there is no witness against her' (במדבר 5:13)
Testimony

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And there is no witness against her,'
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13

phrases.english: meaning: whatever testimony there is against her is enough.
phrases.notes: He means that even one witness is enough for טומאה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְעֵד אֵין בָּהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר from step 19 by quoting a פסוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר that would require two witnesses for טומאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A פסוק says outright that one witness is enough, and a verse overrides logic.

steps.title: A new קל וחומר: maybe one witness is enough for סתירה too
steps.stepSummary: Now that one witness is enough for the serious testimony (טומאה), the משנה argues that the lighter testimony (סתירה) should surely need only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now make a קל וחומר for the first testimony. The final testimony forbids her forever, and still one witness is enough for it. The first testimony does not forbid her forever. So surely one witness should be enough for it too!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the argument around. It uses the result of step 20 to suggest that סתירה also needs only one witness. This sets up the next move, where a verse will block this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 19 the קל וחומר went from light to serious: סתירה needs two, so טומאה should need two. Now it runs the other way: טומאה, the more serious one, needs only one, so סתירה, the lighter one, should need only one. This is a challenge to the rule that סתירה needs two witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a more serious one, or the reverse
The first testimony, about סתירה (being alone with the man)
The final testimony, about טומאה (that she sinned)
A permanent prohibition
One witness

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two testimonies. 'First' means סתירה, which only makes her temporarily forbidden. 'Final' means טומאה, which forbids her forever.

phrases.english: And now, a קל וחומר for the first testimony:
Just as the final testimony,
which forbids her forever,
is established with one witness,
then the first testimony,
which does not forbid her forever,
is it not logical that it should be established with one witness?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר לְעֵדוּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 20 (one witness for טומאה) to build a reverse קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that סתירה needs two witnesses.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the more serious testimony needs only one witness, the less serious one should not need more.

steps.title: The word 'דבר' shows that סתירה needs two witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה blocks the new קל וחומר with a גזרה שוה. The word 'דבר' in the פרשה of divorce matches 'דבר' in the פסוק about two witnesses, so סתירה needs two.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'because he found in her an unseemly matter (דבר).' And elsewhere it says: 'by the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses a matter (דבר) shall be established.' Just as the 'matter' there needs two witnesses, so too here it needs two.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shuts down the קל וחומר from step 21. It links two פסוקים that share the word 'דבר' to show that סתירה needs two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזרה שוה connects the 'דבר' about a woman's improper behavior with the 'דבר' that needs two witnesses. Since a verse teaches the rule, the קל וחומר cannot override it. So the משנה ends up with two witnesses for סתירה and one for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: An unseemly matter (improper behavior)
There, in another place in the תורה
A matter shall be established
Learning from the same word used in two places

steps.whatToRemember: As the משנה is worded, סתירה needs two witnesses (from 'דבר') and טומאה needs only one (from 'ועד אין בה'). The גמרא is about to question the 'דבר' source for סתירה (steps 23 and 24).

phrases.english: The verse states: 'because he found in her an unseemly matter,'
phrases.notes: דברים 24:1

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״כִּי מָצָא בָהּ עֶרְוַת דָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 21 with a גזרה שוה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The קל וחומר that one witness should be enough for סתירה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A גזרה שוה from 'דבר' requires two witnesses, and a verse overrides logic.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is where the משנה gets its basic rule for סתירה. The next step of the גמרא challenges exactly this source.

steps.title: Why not learn two witnesses for סתירה from the word 'בה'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה used 'דבר' as its source. The word 'בה' already teaches that one witness is enough only for טומאה, and not for קינוי or סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this learned from 'because he found in her an unseemly matter'? It is learned from 'בה' (against her): 'against her', meaning טומאה, and not for קינוי. 'Against her', and not for סתירה. That is the source it should have used!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now speaks for itself and challenges the משנה's source. It points out that the word 'בה' already gives the rule that סתירה needs two witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (on 2b) the גמרא read 'ועד אין בה' as limiting the single-witness rule to טומאה only. That limit already tells us that קינוי and סתירה need two witnesses. So the גזרה שוה from 'דבר' seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived (from)
The husband's warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man
Her being alone in private with that man

steps.title: The משנה Really Means the Source Is 'בה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה does mean to learn from 'בה': one witness counts only for טומאה, not for קינוי and not for סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is also what he is saying: the verse says 'בה', against her. With regard to it (טומאה), but not with regard to the warning. With regard to it, but not with regard to the seclusion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23 by agreeing with it. The משנה really does mean that the word 'בה' is the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the גמרא asked why the משנה needed 'דבר' when 'בה' already limits the one-witness rule to טומאה. The answer is that the משנה should be read as using 'בה'. So סתירה needs two witnesses because 'בה' leaves it out, not because of the גזרה שוה.

steps.title: Where Do We Learn That Plain Defilement Needs Two Witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that one witness is not believed about טומאה when there was no קינוי and no סתירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for defilement in general, without a warning and without seclusion, from where do we know that one witness is not believed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It is setting up the next step, where the 'דבר' teaching will find its real use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ועד אין בה' only makes one witness enough in a full סוטה case, after קינוי and סתירה. When there was no warning and no seclusion, the question is what makes one witness not enough for טומאה.

steps.title: The 'דבר' Comparison Teaches Two Witnesses for Plain Defilement
steps.stepSummary: The word 'דבר' in the divorce פסוק is matched to 'דבר' in the two-witness פסוק. So plain טומאה needs two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says: 'Because he found in her an unseemly matter (דבר).' There it says: 'By the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall a matter (דבר) be established.' Just as the 'matter' there needs two witnesses, so too here it needs two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 25 with the גזרה שוה of 'דבר'. Plain טומאה needs two witnesses, like any other matter in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The divorce פסוק talks about a husband finding 'ערות דבר', something improper, in his wife. Because it shares the word 'דבר' with the general rule of two witnesses, a claim of טומאה with no סוטה process also needs two. The גזרה שוה from step 22 now has its proper job.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two פסוקים

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same 'דבר' גזרה שוה from step 22. It is no longer the source for סתירה ('בה' covers that now). It now teaches about plain טומאה with no קינוי and no סתירה.
steps.whatToRemember: 'בה' teaches that one witness is enough only for טומאה inside a סוטה case. 'דבר' teaches that טומאה outside a סוטה case needs two witnesses.

steps.title: A ברייתא Defines First and Final Testimony
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the משנה's terms: the 'first testimony' is testimony about סתירה, and the 'final testimony' is testimony about טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Which is the first testimony? This is testimony about seclusion. The final testimony is testimony about defilement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that tells us what the משנה means by 'first testimony' and 'final testimony'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה from step 19 spoke of a 'first' and a 'final' testimony without naming them. The ברייתא names them: first is סתירה, which leads to the bitter water, and final is טומאה, which forbids her forever. This confirms how steps 19 to 26 read the משנה.
